task: jepa.cpp inference timing and memory on one CUDA device, tools/jepa-bench --gpu on synthetic deterministic input

protocol.ms: wall time of ggml_backend_graph_compute for the named graph (jepa_context_last_compute_ms); model load, graph build/alloc, the host-side patchify and the output copy — PCIe transfers on this backend — are excluded
protocol.wall_ms: the full public-API call, including all of the above
protocol.ms_mean/ms_min/ms_std: over `repeat` measured runs after `warmup` unmeasured ones; ggml's CUDA backend captures a CUDA graph once it has seen the same topology and tensor addresses twice, so warmup >= 2 is what makes the measured runs the captured path
protocol.gpu_prec: the accumulation precision of every mul_mat: f32 = GGML_PREC_F32, f16 = cuBLAS' own compute type. Which one a GPU context picks is per family (src/jepa.cpp, jepa_gpu_prec_f32_default) and both settings are parity-measured per family in tests/results/gpu-prec.json; $JEPA_GPU_PREC and --gpu-prec override the family's choice for a process
protocol.gpu_prec_explicit: false = the family's own default, i.e. the shipping configuration; true = --gpu-prec asked for the other setting
protocol.kv: K/V dtype in flash attention; auto is F32 for f32 files and F16 otherwise
protocol.encoder_ms: head/predictor rows only: the faster of two warm encoder passes that produced this row's input (a third, cold one runs first and is discarded)
protocol.tokens_per_s: tokens / ms_mean; for lewm-rollout ms is per step and tokens is 1, so the rate is steps/s
protocol.peak_rss_mib: process VmHWM after the run — host memory, not device memory
protocol.ftype: the type requested at conversion time (the GGUF filename suffix)
protocol.cpu_f16_t32_ms: ms_mean of the same graph and shape at f16 on 32 CPU threads, from tests/results/benchmarks.json
protocol.grid: the configurations docs/performance.md tabulates (scripts/bench_gpu.grid); a cell printed as a dash there is one nobody has asked for, not one that failed
protocol.device: per row, and authoritative: this artifact spans more than one card, so there is deliberately no top-level device index

pytorch_gpu.task: PyTorch encoder forward on one GPU, the baseline docs/performance.md compares jepa.cpp CUDA against

protocol.timing: 3 warmup + 7 timed forwards, cuda.synchronize() around each
protocol.attn_implementation: sdpa where the model accepts it (LeVJEPA ships its own code)
protocol.input: the stored preprocessed tensor of a reference fixture — the same pixels jepa.cpp is timed on
protocol.vjepa2: skip_predictor=True, so the forward is the encoder alone
protocol.ms: mean/min/median/std over the timed forwards of the full model call

pytorch_gpu_batched.task: PyTorch encoder forward on one GPU, the baseline docs/performance.md compares jepa.cpp CUDA against

protocol.timing: 3 warmup + 7 timed forwards, cuda.synchronize() around each
protocol.batch: per row; the fixture tensor repeated along the batch axis, the axis jepa-bench --batch sweeps
protocol.attn_implementation: sdpa where the model accepts it (LeVJEPA ships its own code)
protocol.input: the stored preprocessed tensor of a reference fixture — the same pixels jepa.cpp is timed on
protocol.vjepa2: skip_predictor=True, so the forward is the encoder alone
protocol.ms: mean/min/median/std over the timed forwards of the full model call
protocol.runtime: eager, or compile for a torch.compile'd module warmed up before timing (mode='default'); the compile itself is not in the milliseconds
